Rashi on Pesachim 38a:10:1.hebrew: או דילמא הואיל ואילו לא קרא עליה שם חלה אית לה היתר במושבות - אם נטמא ונפיק, השתא נמי לא פקע תורת מצה מינה משום קריאת שם חלה, דהא חלה בעלמא לא נפקא מכלל מצה, כדתנן מתניתין ״והכהנים בחלה״. אלא הא לחודה משום דאסורה ליה במושבות, ואמרינן ״הואיל״ ונפיק:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:10:1.english: Or perhaps, since, if he had not designated it with the name challah, it would have permissibility in [all] habitations - if it became ritually impure, and he could fulfill [his obligation with it], now too, the status of matzah does not depart from it on account of the designation of the name challah, for ordinary challah is not excluded from the category of matzah, as we learned in the Mishnah: "and the priests with challah." Rather, this [case] alone [is in doubt] because it is forbidden to him in [all] habitations, and we say "since," and he fulfills [his obligation].

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:11:1.hebrew: הלקוח בכסף מעשר שני - בירושלים, כדכתיב: "ונתתה הכסף בכל אשר תאוה נפשך" וגו':
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:11:1.english: That which was purchased with second-tithe money - In Jerusalem, as it is written: "And you shall spend the money on whatever your soul desires," etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:12:1.hebrew: ואליבא דרבנן - דפליגי עליה דרבי יהודה ואמרי לקוח בכסף מעשר שנטמא יפדה, דאלימא למיתפס פדיונו, לא תיבעי לך. דאף על גב דהך חלה לית לה היתר במושבות — דכל זמן שלא נטמא אין לה פדייה בירושלים, ומשנטמא שוב אין לה היתר אכילה, דהא חלה היא — אפילו הכי אמרינן: הואיל ואילו לא קרא עליה שם הוה לה היתר במושבות על ידי טומאה, דנפיק בה אף בירושלים, השתא נמי נפיק, כדאמרן במעשר גופיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:12:1.english: And in accordance with the Rabbis - who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda and say [that something] purchased with [second-]tithe money that became ritually impure may be redeemed, for it is strong enough to take hold of its redemption, do not raise the dilemma. For even though this challah has no permission [to be eaten] in [all] dwelling places — since as long as it has not become ritually impure it has no redemption in Jerusalem, and once it has become ritually impure it no longer has permission to be eaten, for it is challah — even so, we say: since if he had not designated it [as challah] it would have had permission [to be eaten] in [all] dwelling places through ritual impurity, so that he could fulfill [his obligation] with it even in Jerusalem, now too he fulfills [his obligation], as we said regarding [second] tithe itself.

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:12:2.hebrew: יקבר - כל לקוח בכסף מעשר שני שנטמא, משום דקלישא קדושתיה ולא אלים למיתפס פדיוניה. ואי נמי לא קרא עליה שם חלה, לא הוה ליה היתר במושבות:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:12:2.english: It must be buried - [This refers to] anything purchased with second-tithe money that became ritually impure, because its sanctity is weak and it is not strong [enough] to take hold of its redemption [money]. And even if one did not designate challah upon it, it would have no permissibility in the settlements [outside Jerusalem].

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:14:1.hebrew: מאי מי אמרינן הואיל ואי לאו לקוח הוא - כלומר, הואיל ומעשר שני גופיה, דאתי האי מחמתיה וקיל האי מיניה, נפקינן במצה דידיה — דאית ליה היתר במושבות על ידי טומאה — והא דלית ליה היתר להאי, לאו חומרא הוא לגביה, אלא קולא הוא, משום דלא אלים למיתפס פדיונו, הלכך לא חמיר כדמעיקרא; ואי משום דחלה הוא ובלאו לקוח נמי לית ליה היתר, הכא נמי נימא הואיל אחרינא: הואיל ואילו לא קרא עליה שם ולא לקוח הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:14:1.english: What [is the meaning of,] "Do we say, since if it were not purchased" - That is to say: since [with] second tithe itself — from which this [purchased produce] derives and than which this [purchased produce] is more lenient — we fulfill [our obligation] with its matzah, because it has permissibility in [all] habitations through ritual impurity; and the fact that this [purchased produce] has no permissibility [via redemption] is not a stringency regarding it, rather it is a leniency, because it is not strong enough to transfer its sanctity to redemption [money], and therefore it is not as stringent as the original [second tithe]. And if [the difficulty is] because it is challah, so that even without being purchased [with second-tithe money] it has no permissibility [in all habitations], here too we say another "since": since if one had not designated it [as challah] and it were not purchased [with second-tithe money, it would be permitted in all habitations].

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:15:1.hebrew: או דילמא חד הואיל אמרינן - כגון חלת מעשר גופיה, דלא נפקי בה אלא ע"י הואיל ואי לא קרא עליה שם, אי נמי חולין של לקוח, לא נפקי בה אלא ע"י הואיל ואי לאו לקוח הוא — התם אמרינן הואיל ושרי. אבל חלת לקוח, דבעי תרי הואיל, לא אמרי'. וא"ת: בחלת מעשר גופיה נמי תרי הואיל איכא — הואיל ואי לא קרא עליה שם, והואיל ואי מיטמא פריק לה ואית ליה היתר במושבות? הכא לא קרינא הואיל, דבר שיש בידו לעשות לגרום לה טומאה מיד ופריק:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:15:1.english: Or perhaps we say one "since" - For example, challah of [second] tithe itself, with which one does not fulfill [his obligation] except by means of "since if he had not designated a name upon it [as challah]"; or alternatively, non-sacred [produce] purchased [with second-tithe money], with which one does not fulfill [his obligation] except by means of "since if it had not been purchased [with second-tithe money]" — there we say "since," and it is permitted. But [regarding] challah of [produce] purchased [with second-tithe money], which requires two "since"s, we do not say [it]. And if you will say: In [the case of] challah of [second] tithe itself, too, there are two "since"s — "since if he had not designated a name upon it," and "since if it becomes impure, he can redeem it and it has permissibility in [all] dwellings"? Here we do not call [that] a "since," [as it is] something that is in his power to do — to cause it impurity immediately and redeem [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:15:2.hebrew: מסתברא שם מעשר חד הוא - וכי היכי דנפיק במעשר גופיה, נפיק בחלתו, הואיל ושם חלה לא נפיק בעלמא מכלל מצה. ונפיק נמי בחלת הלקוח, דהא מכח מעשר באה, ולא מחמרינן ליה מיניה:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:15:2.english: It stands to reason [that] the category of tithe is a single [designation] - And just as one fulfills [his obligation] with the tithe itself, he fulfills [it] with its challah, since the category of challah is not excluded in general from the category of matzah. And he also fulfills [his obligation] with the challah of [produce] purchased [with second-tithe money], for it comes by virtue of the tithe, and we do not treat it more stringently than [the tithe] itself.

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:1:1.hebrew: ומצה של מעשר כו' לדברי ר"מ אין אדם יוצא בה - ואפילו לא דריש עוני לשון אנינות, בעינן מצה שלו ולא של גבוה. ולקמן פריך: מי כתיב מצתכם:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:1:1.english: And matzah of [second] tithe, etc., according to Rabbi Meir, a person cannot fulfill [his obligation] with it - Even if he does not expound "oni" [affliction] as an expression of aninut [mourning], we [still] require matzah that is his own, and not [the property] of the Most High. And later on, [the Gemara] asks: Is "your matzah" written?

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:7:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר - לימא מסייעא הא לכל מילתיה דרב אסי, דמדבהא פליגי, באתרוג נמי פליגי:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:7:1.english: This is what [it] is saying - Let us say that this supports the entire statement of Rav Assi, for since they disagree regarding this [matter], they also disagree regarding an etrog.

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:7:2.hebrew: תרי זימני - אבל התם, "לכם" למעוטי שאול וגזול; אבל אתרוג של מעשר שני, האי דאיתיהיב ליה לאכילה, נפיק ביה, ואפילו לר"מ:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:7:2.english: Twice - But there [regarding the citron], [the word] "for yourselves" [serves only] to exclude a borrowed or stolen [citron]; however, [with] a citron of second tithe, since it is given to him for eating, he fulfills [his obligation] with it, even according to Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:8:1.english: [In accordance with the opinion] of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili - Who said above, "Excluded is this [second tithe], which is not eaten in [a state of] acute mourning."

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:8:2.hebrew: בחולין - לאחר שנטלה חלתו, לא נפיק בחולין דידיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:8:2.english: With [the] non-sacred [portion] - After its challah has been taken, one does not fulfill [his obligation] with its non-sacred [portion].

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:8:3.hebrew: כי תיבעי לך לר"ע - דלא דריש אוני, ומיהו היתר במושבות בעי, כדמיעט לעיל בכורים מהאי טעמא. ומעשר שני ריבה משום דאית ביה היתר מושבות אפי' לאחר שנכנס לירושלים אם נטמא, כרבי אלעזר:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:8:3.english: When you raise the dilemma, [it is] according to Rabbi Akiva - For he does not expound [the term] oni; however, he does require [that it be] permitted in [all] dwelling places, just as he excluded first fruits earlier for this reason. And he included second tithe because it has permissibility in [all] dwelling places even after it has entered Jerusalem, if it became ritually impure, in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.

Rashi on Pesachim 38a:9:1.hebrew: לשריפה אזלה - דתרומה טמאה אסורה באכילה, ובעודה טהורה אין לה היתר במושבות, משום דמעשר שני הוא, ובתר דקלטוה מחיצות לית ליה פדייה:
Rashi on Pesachim 38a:9:1.english: It goes for burning - For impure terumah is forbidden to be eaten; and while it is pure, it is not permitted [to be eaten] in [all] habitations because it is second tithe, and once the walls [of Jerusalem] have taken it in, it has no redemption.

Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:10:1.hebrew: או דילמא הואיל ואילו לא קרי לה שם - תימה לר"י: אי אמרת "הואיל", א"כ בכורים נמי נאכלין בכל מושבותיכם, הואיל ולא קרי ליה שם. וי"ל דלא דמי: דשם בכורים אינו נאכל בכל מושבותיכם, אבל הכא שם חלה נאכל בכל מושבותיכם, וכן שם מעשר לחודיה נאכל בכל מושבותיכם; הלכך בחלת מעשר אמר שפיר "הואיל ולא קרי לה שם". ועוד הקשה: אי אמרת "הואיל", מעשר שני נמי נאכל בכל מושבותיכם, הואיל ולא העלהו לירושלים, ואמאי איצטריך לאוקמא לעיל (פסחים דף לו:) כרבי אלעזר? וי"ל דאי לאו משום דר' אלעזר, לא חשיב שם מעשר שני נאכל בכל מושבותיכם משום ד"הואיל ולא העלהו לירושלים", כמו שאין לומר "הואיל ולא קרא לו שם מעשר":
Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:10:1.english: Or perhaps, since if one had not designated it [as ḥalla] - It is astonishing to Rabbi Yitzḥak: If you say "since" [one could have avoided its current sanctity], if so, [one should also be able to fulfill the obligation of matza with] bikkurim (first fruits), [as they too would be considered] eaten in all your habitations, since one did not designate them [as bikkurim]. And one can answer that it is not comparable: for the category of bikkurim is not eaten in all your habitations, whereas here, the category of ḥalla is eaten in all your habitations, and similarly, the category of tithe (ma'aser) by itself is eaten in all your habitations; therefore, in the case of ḥalla of tithe, one can properly say, "since one did not designate it [as ḥalla]." And he [Rabbi Yitzḥak] asked further: If you say "since," [then] second tithe (ma'aser sheni) too [should be considered] eaten in all your habitations, since he has not [yet] brought it up to Jerusalem [and could redeem it]; so why was it necessary to establish [the ruling] above (Pesachim 36b) in accordance with Rabbi Elazar? And one can answer that were it not for [the view of] Rabbi Elazar, the category of second tithe would not be considered eaten in all your habitations on the basis of "since he has not brought it up to Jerusalem," just as one cannot say "since he did not designate it as tithe."

Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:13:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר יקבר - טעמיה דר' יהודה משום דדריש: כסף ראשון ולא כסף שני, ולכך אינו נפדה לקוח טהור ברחוק מקום, וה"ה שאין נפדה טמא בקרוב מקום, דתרוייהו מחד קרא נפקי — מ"לא תוכל שאתו". ורבנן לא דרשי כסף ראשון ולא כסף שני, וסברי דלקוח טהור נפדה ברחוק מקום, וה"ה טמא בקרוב מקום. וקשה לרשב"א, דבריש איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף מט.) פריך: ולא מצינו שטפל חמור מן העיקר, והרי מעשר הוא נפדה ולקוח אינו נפדה, דתנן "הלקוח שנטמא יפדה" — נטמא אין, לא נטמא לא, והיינו ברחוק מקום, דכה"ג מעשר עצמו נפדה, ובע"א לא הוי טפל חמור מן העיקר; אלמא לקוח לרבנן נמי אינו נפדה טהור ברחוק מקום! ותירץ ר"י דהתם מיירי מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:13:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It should be buried - Rabbi Yehuda's reason is that he expounds: "first money, and not second money"; therefore, ritually pure [produce] purchased [with second-tithe money] is not redeemed in a distant place, and the same applies that ritually impure [purchased produce] is not redeemed in a nearby place, since both of them derive from one verse — from "you are unable to carry it." But the Rabbis do not expound "first money, and not second money," and they hold that ritually pure purchased [produce] is redeemed in a distant place, and the same applies [to] ritually impure [purchased produce] in a nearby place. And this is difficult for Rashba, for at the beginning of [the chapter] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 49a), [the Gemara] asks: "Have we not found that the subordinate [item] is more stringent than the primary [item]? Behold, [second] tithe itself is redeemed, whereas [produce] purchased [with second-tithe money] is not redeemed, as we learned in a Mishnah: '[Produce] purchased [with second-tithe money] that became ritually impure should be redeemed' — [implying that if] it became ritually impure, yes [it is redeemed]; [if] it did not become ritually impure, no [it is not redeemed]!" And this [refers to] a distant place, since in such a case [second] tithe itself is redeemed, whereas otherwise the subordinate would not be more stringent than the primary; thus [we see that] even according to the Rabbis, ritually pure purchased [produce] is not redeemed in a distant place! And R"I answered that there it is speaking by Rabbinic law.

Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:16:1.hebrew: חלות תודה ורקיקי נזיר - נראה לר"י כפ"ה, דמיירי שלא נשחט עליהם הזבח ולא הוקדשו, דאי הוקדשו — תיפוק ליה דבעינן "מצתכם", דגמרינן לעיל "לחם" "לחם". ועוד, דקאמר "למכור בשוק יוצאין בהן", משמע דבלא הוקדשו מיירי. וה"פ: "מצה המשתמרת לשם מצה, יצאה זו שמשתמרת לשם זבח" — כשיקדישנה. וכן "שאין נאכלין אלא ליום אחד" — אקרא ד"משתמרת" סמיך, דבעינן שתהא נשמרת לשם שבעה. והא דפריך "ותיפוק ליה שאין נאכלין באנינות" ו"שאין נאכלין בכל מושבות", ה"פ: שאין נעשה לאכול בכל מושבותיכם ולאכול באנינות. והא דלא פריך "שאין נעשה להיות מצתכם אלא לגבוה" — כיון דלא כתב בהדיא פסול ד"מצתכם", לא שייך למיפרך הכי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:16:1.english: The loaves of a thanks-offering and the wafers of a nazirite - It appears to Ri [to be] like the explanation of Rashi, that [the Mishnah] is speaking of [a case] where the sacrifice was not slaughtered over them and they were not consecrated; for if they were consecrated, let it be derived from [the fact] that we require "your matza," as we learned above [from the verbal analogy of] "bread" [and] "bread." And furthermore, since [the Mishnah] states, "[If one made them] to sell in the market, one may fulfill his obligation with them," it implies that it is speaking of [a case] where they were not consecrated. And this is its explanation: "Matza that is guarded for the sake of matza — excluded is this [matza], which is guarded for the sake of a sacrifice" — [meaning] when he will consecrate it. And likewise, [the argument] "that they are only eaten for one day" relies on the verse of "guarded," as we require that it be guarded for the sake of seven [days]. And that which [the Gemara] asks, "Let it be derived [from the fact] that they are not eaten in [a state of] acute mourning" and "that they are not eaten in all [your] dwellings," this is its explanation: that it is not made to be eaten in all your dwellings and to be eaten in [a state of] acute mourning. And that which [the Gemara] does not ask, "[Let it be derived] that it is not made to be 'your matza,' but rather for the Most High" — since the disqualification of "your matza" is not written explicitly, it is not appropriate to ask like that.

Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:5:1.hebrew: אתיא לחם לחם. הקשה הר"י דאורלינ"ש: כיון דילפינן "לחם" "לחם" - דבעינן מצה שלכם, אמאי איצטריך לעיל למעוטי שלא יצא בטבל, "מי שאיסורו משום בל תאכל חמץ כו'"? תיפוק ליה דבעי' שלכם, וטבל אינו שלכם! דהא אתרוג של דמאי דמכשרי ב"ה בלולב הגזול (סוכה דף לה:), מפרש התם משום דאי בעי מפקר לנכסיה והוי עני וחזי ליה, השתא נמי "שלכם" קרינן ביה; משמע דטבל גמור לא חשיב שלכם. ותי' ר"י: אתרוג של טבל לא חשיב שלו, כיון שצריך ליתן ממנו לכהן וללוי, ובעינן שיהא כל האתרוג שלו. אבל מצה — שאם אכל כל כך שאם היה נותן ממנו תרומה או מעשר ממה שאכל, אכתי אכל שיעור מצה — חשיב שפיר שלו. ורשב"א תירץ דאיצטריך לעיל קרא להיכא שמה שיפריש יהיה שלו, כגון אם הוא כהן או לוי או ישראל עני, ונטל ממנו ככר תרומה ומעשר ראשון, ד"שלכם" קרינן ביה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:5:1.english: "[This principle] is derived [by a verbal analogy between] 'bread' [and] 'bread.'" — Rabbi Yaakov of Orléans raised a difficulty: Since we derive [from] "bread" [and] "bread" that we require matza that is "yours," why was it necessary earlier to exclude [tevel, teaching] that one does not fulfill his obligation with tevel [from the verse, "only that] whose prohibition is due to 'do not eat chametz,' etc."? Let it be derived from [the fact] that we require "yours," and tevel is not "yours"! For regarding an etrog of demai, which Beit Hillel declare valid in [the chapter] Lulav Hagazul (Sukkah 35b), [the Gemara] explains there [that it is valid] because if he wanted, he could renounce ownership of his property and become a poor person, and it would be fit for him; [therefore,] even now we apply to it [the requirement of] "yours." This implies that full-fledged tevel is not considered "yours." And Ri answered: An etrog of tevel is not considered his, because one must give from it to a Kohen and to a Levite, and we require that the entire etrog be his. However, matza — where if he ate so much that even if he were to give from it terumah or tithe from what he ate, he would still have eaten the [minimum] measure of matza — is properly considered his. And Rashba answered that the verse earlier is necessary for a case where what he will separate will [still] be his, such as if he is a Kohen, a Levite, or a poor Israelite, and he took from it a loaf of terumah and first tithe, to which we apply "yours."

Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:9:1.hebrew: אבל חלתו דאי מטמיא - זו הסוגיא כמ"ד (מכות דף כ.) מחיצה לקלוט דאורייתא; דאי מדרבנן, יש לה היתר מושבות, דאי יצאה חוץ למחיצה, נפדית אפילו טהורה. אי נמי: כיון דמדרבנן אין להם פדייה, לא חשיב נאכל בכל מושבות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 38a:9:1.english: "However, its ḥalla, which if it becomes ritually impure..." - This sugya accords with the one who says (Makkot 20a) [that] a partition taking hold is biblical; for if [it were] rabbinic, it would have a permit [to be eaten] in [all] habitations, since if it went outside the partition, it could be redeemed even when ritually pure. Alternatively: since rabbinically they have no redemption, it is not considered "[something that can be] eaten in all habitations."
